It exposes utilities to trigger browser downloads of text and binary data, and to open the browser file picker to read selected files as either text or bytes. The implementation is built on top of the web package and the browser DOM/File APIs, handing blobs to the browser for download, using an input element to invoke the file picker, and using a FileReader to read chosen files back into Dart as text or an ArrayBuffer.

Utility functions are asynchronous where appropriate, returning null when the user cancels the picker or when the selected file is too large or cannot be read in the requested form.

This file defines the referral reward model and the logic used to interpret how granted referral rewards affect product features. It declares an enum of server-known rewards (ReferralReward) with stable string identifiers that match the server schema, and a final abstract utility class (ReferralRewards) that codifies the referral program rules: how many referrals are required, a temporary welcome-gift window for invited users, which rewards outright unlock locked features, and which reward grants increased limits for count-limited features.

The ReferralRewards class exposes purely static constants and helper methods to compute gift expiry, check whether a gift is active, map rewards to opened features, compute raised allowances for specific features, and produce the list of features impacted by a reward. These members are designed to be consumed by higher-level billing or feature-checking code so the app can decide whether a given set of granted rewards should open features or increase limits for the current user.

overview.summary:
This module centralizes quota and allowance logic used by the application to determine usage limits for AI answers and OCR scans. It defines typed plan identifiers and window types, concrete allowance records for free and pro plans, trial-specific allowances and cost ceilings, and daily limits based on an account's trust level. The module exposes a set of utility functions to coerce stored plan values, compute an account's effective plan (including a beta override), detect trial status, compute plan or trial allowances for different usage kinds, and produce a QuotaInfo structure that represents what the app shows the user about their allowance.

The file groups related constants and small helpers so callers can reason about lifetime vs monthly windows, per-plan limits, trial fallbacks, new-account reductions, and monthly AI cost ceilings. It also includes helpers to compute reduced allowances for new accounts and to express trust tiers such as paid, established, or new, and how those tiers map to daily usage caps.

This module implements a Supabase Edge Function for handling account deletion related checks and billing considerations. It defines a SubRow interface representing subscription state (active, trialing, past due, and not set to end) and exposes two module-level utility functions: lastSignInMs, which derives the caller's last sign-in time from the verified session JWT's amr claim, and bills, which performs billing-related logic before account deletion. The implementation integrates shared helpers for CORS and JSON responses, authentication (including requireUserId and service client access), and usage rate limiting, indicating this code is intended to run as a protected, rate-limited HTTP handler that enforces recent reauthentication and inspects subscription status before proceeding with account deletion actions.

overview.summary: This SQL file implements a referral system for a Supabase-backed application. It defines tables to store one referral code per user (referral_codes), a single record for each invited account linking the invitee to their referrer (referrals), and a table of rewards granted to users (reward_grants). The file provides SQL and PL/pgSQL functions to enumerate available rewards, compute how many reward picks a referral count entitles a user to, create or return a caller's referral code, record a claim of a referral code by a newly created account, and mark an invited account as activated when they confirm their email. Access is restricted so clients can only read their own referral codes and granted rewards; writes are performed via the provided functions running with defined security settings.

overview.summary:
This SQL file performs a full, single-transaction setup of the SmartBudget database schema and reference data for a Supabase/PostgreSQL deployment. It creates required extensions and core tables (for example, currencies, exchange_rates, and profiles), declares constraints and foreign keys (including references to auth.users), and seeds a comprehensive set of currency rows with localized names, symbols, and decimal precision. The file is designed to be idempotent where practical, using conditional creation statements and conflict-handling to update existing reference rows without duplicating data.

The script also encodes design notes and conventions used across the application: monetary values are stored as integer minor units plus a currency code, user-owned tables carry user_id and rely on Row-Level Security, and profiles are populated with defaults (locale, theme, base currency, plan). It begins the setup inside a transaction and includes indexes, default timestamp columns, UUID primary keys generated by gen_random_uuid(), and seeded reference data required for the application to function (notably the full set of supported currencies).

overview.summary:
This file provides a lightweight fake Supabase test harness and helpers for use in tests. It exports a Q class plus a set of module-level utility functions that simulate common Supabase behaviors: creating a test client, resolving or failing promises, reserving resources, constructing SQL literals for call arguments, delivering subscription events, and interacting with a Postgres-like test environment. A SupabaseClient type alias is present (typed as any) and createClient produces a client instance suitable for test scenarios.

Several functions are asynchronous and intended to model remote interactions: applySubscriptionEvent and onPostgres run async workflows against the fake environment, and getUser parses an authorization header such as "Bearer user-<id>" to return the corresponding user or Postgres account representation. The file centralizes utilities that make it straightforward to simulate authentication, database callbacks, and real-time subscription events in unit and integration tests that depend on Supabase-like semantics.

overview.summary:
This TypeScript test module contains a collection of standalone helper functions and test utilities used by the supabase/functions test suite. It defines 16 module-level functions that perform tasks such as generating payloads or headers (ask, askBody, cfg, b64, jwt), manipulating test state (calls, last, lastPlan, scan, nextMonth, before, stuckUsed), and executing asynchronous test flows (checkout, yearly, del). The file also performs numerous environment variable manipulations at module load time to configure timeouts, API endpoints, promotional windows, and test user IDs for external services like PayPal and Whop, which are important for shaping the test environment for payment- and subscription-related scenarios.

The utilities are designed to be used directly by tests to create and examine test conditions, simulate checkout flows, and manage mock or integration interactions with outbound services. Several functions are asynchronous to accommodate remote or time-dependent operations, and the module-level environment setup indicates that tests relying on these utilities expect to run with specific external API URLs and feature flags configured dynamically during the test run.

Verify SheetTable interpretation for Excel workbooks (.xlsx) including type detection for numeric/date cells and that StatementParser.guess and StatementParser.read produce correct results.

Tests cover internationalization scenarios: locale-specific headers, number and date formats, and right-to-left language content.
overview.summary: This file is a Dart test suite exercising the statement import and table reading functionality used by the application. It defines a local helper (readCsv) that converts CSV text into a SheetTable via TableReader, runs StatementParser.guess to detect header/column layouts, and then calls StatementParser.read to produce StatementRead objects for assertions. The tests cover CSV parsing edge cases (quoted fields, different separators, legacy encodings), workbook detection and size limits, and parsing of bank statement formats (various languages, date and number formats, signed vs unsigned amounts, and columns that indicate credit/debit). Several tests validate that parsed StatementRow entries have the expected dates, amounts, transaction types, categories, and unreadable-row counts.
